Data.title: Bitcoin Price Analysis: Is the September Rally Structure in Danger as BTC Hangs by a Thread?
Data.body: Bitcoin is attempting to stabilize around $78K after posting its fourth straight weekly loss, with sentiment weighed down by the record Binance hack and a $643.3 million withdrawal from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs on Friday. The asset now sits inside a key demand zone that could decide whether the September rally structure survives. Meanwhile, the Velocity metric has climbed to its highest level since late 2024, suggesting that supply is circulating more actively even as prices decline. Bitcoin Price Analysis: The Daily Chart On the daily timeframe, Bitcoin continues to trade within the broad ascending channel that has guided the recovery from the summer lows near $58K. However, the rejection from the upper boundary and the $86K–$90K supply zone in late September has given way to a series of lower highs, and last week’s sell-off pushed BTC below the channel’s midline around $82K. The price is now trading inside the $75K–$78K order block, which formed the base of the sharp September rally. The lower wick printed during the hack-driven drop shows buyers responding here, but the rebound has so far been shallow. Holding this zone would allow BTC to attempt a return toward the channel midline and, eventually, the $86K–$90K supply zone. Conversely, a daily candle closing below $75K would expose the channel’s lower boundary near $73K. A breakdown through that confluence would invalidate the structure that has carried the price higher since mid-year and raise the risk of a deeper correction. For now, the channel remains intact, but sellers clearly control short-term momentum. BTC/USDT 4-Hour Chart The 4-hour chart offers a clearer view of the deterioration. Bitcoin broke below the lower boundary of its orange ascending channel around October 23, and the subsequent rebound stalled inside the $80K-$82K supply zone, effectively retesting the broken trendline from below. That rejection was followed by a sharp sell-off as news of the Binance breach hit the market. Buyers stepped in at the $76K demand zone, which sits within the daily order block, and the price has since recovered toward $79K before easing back to around $78K. A sustained move above $79K could bring the $80K-$82K supply zone back into play, while reclaiming it would open the way toward $85K, where the last significant rebound was rejected. On the downside, losing $76K would likely trigger a test of the lower edge of demand near $75K, the last support before the daily channel’s lower boundary. Until BTC reclaims the broken channel, the short-term structure favors sellers, with rebounds likely to meet overhead supply. On-Chain Analysis Velocity on CryptoQuant measures how quickly coins circulate through the network relative to the total supply, applying the economic concept of money velocity to on-chain activity. Rising readings indicate that coins are changing hands more frequently, while declining readings point to long-term holding behavior and supply moving into dormant addresses. The metric fell steadily from roughly 15.8 in early 2024 to around 12.1 in October 2025, a period in which Bitcoin rallied to its all-time high near $125K. That combination reflected classic scarcity dynamics, with a growing share of supply held off the market. Since then, the trend has reversed, with velocity rising to approximately 14.6 even as the price dropped sharply. This divergence suggests that previously idle coins are re-entering circulation, a pattern more consistent with redistribution than accumulation, and one that weakens the supply-squeeze dynamic behind the 2025 rally. However, velocity alone cannot reveal who is buying or selling. If it keeps climbing while BTC struggles below $82K, the $75K order block would likely face increasing pressure, which could reverse the whole BTC price rebound since summer. The chart spans from 2017 to a projected 2032 and layers multiple technical frameworks to build a case that XRP is entering Wave 3 of a major Elliott Wave sequence. His message to anyone who can interpret it is simple: “If you understand the Elliott Wave structure , you’re one step ahead.” The Wave Count Elliott Wave Theory organizes price movement into five-wave impulse sequences. The analyst applies this across two degrees simultaneously. The larger structure shows a completed five-wave cycle bottoming around 2020. A new five-wave impulse is now developing inside Wave 3 of that larger sequence, which is what he calls the biggest Wave 3 . XRP currently trades near $1.25, sitting just above the $1.10 level the analyst identifies as a critical near-term base. A deeper support floor sits at $0.95. The Fibonacci ratios listed on the chart govern each wave. Wave 3 extends to 161.8% of Wave 1. A “Most Sell-Off Region” near $5.43 marks where significant selling pressure is expected before the final wave pushes higher. Two Measured Move indicators project prior price swings forward to validate target ranges. Multiple diagonal trend lines form an ascending channel containing XRP’s price action since 2017, with the asset currently near its lower boundary. The Timeline The Wave 3 structure plays out between 2025 and 2029, with the full cycle concluding around 2031 to 2032. The sub-waves inside the orange box on his chart are already labeled, showing the anticipated oscillations within that move. Data.title: Anchorpoint Plans Native HKDAP on Solana as Hong Kong Dollar Access Expands
Data.body: TL;DR Anchorpoint announced its Solana collaboration on October 30. Native minting and redemption are planned capabilities. The issuer still describes HKDAP as being in Beta Access. Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issuer Anchorpoint plans to bring HKDAP to Solana through a collaboration announced on October 30. The proposed expansion would give the token a native route into another blockchain ecosystem, with payments and tokenized-asset transactions among the intended uses. Anchorpoint’s official release describes planned native minting and redemption. It does not announce that public Solana issuance or unrestricted retail access has already begun. A Hong Kong dollar balance closer to its users A stablecoin tied to the Hong Kong dollar could be useful when the payment, investment or accounting obligation is denominated in that currency. Holding a dollar token referenced to a different currency can add a conversion step and expose the user to exchange-rate movements before the final payment is made. Placing the instrument on a network already used by a potential customer changes the access problem. A wallet or application would not necessarily need to send users to another chain before they could settle a Hong Kong dollar obligation. The business case depends on actual demand for that currency within the ecosystem. A new network listing does not create a payment corridor by itself. Merchants, investment platforms and counterparties still need reasons to receive the token and dependable ways to use or redeem it. Native issuance changes one part of the risk chain A native token is issued on the destination network under the issuer’s arrangements. A bridged representation adds a mechanism linking an asset in one location to a representation elsewhere. Those architectures place responsibility for transfers and backing in different places. For a treasury team, that distinction affects reconciliation. The team needs to establish what it owns, which entity owes redemption and how to identify the genuine asset. A familiar ticker displayed in a wallet is insufficient evidence of any of those points. The proposed Solana route would therefore need clear contract information, supported custody and a documented operational path. None of those implementation questions is answered merely by the speed with which the underlying chain can confirm a transaction. Beta access remains the relevant starting point Anchorpoint’s current FAQ says Beta Access is live through selected authorized distributors for non-retail users, with HKDAP available on Ethereum during that stage. Full Launch is targeted as early as the end of 2026, subject to readiness across issuance, distribution and supporting infrastructure. That sequencing matters because a technical integration and a customer rollout can progress on different schedules. An issuer may test issuance, while a distributor is still preparing onboarding or a wallet provider is checking how to display the asset. Retail expansion also brings a different support burden. Institutions can negotiate workflows and coordinate directly with counterparties. A broader user base needs understandable transaction status, fees, recovery procedures and reliable routes for reporting a problem. Distribution will decide whether the rail is used The meaningful milestone would be a named, operational service showing how a user obtains HKDAP, transacts with it and exits back into usable bank money when needed. A complete journey is more informative than the number of potential wallet integrations. Liquidity matters throughout that journey. A payment network may operate continuously while currency conversion or redemption capacity is constrained at certain times. Users care about the completed payment, including its total cost, rather than only the blockchain leg. Anchorpoint’s plan is therefore best understood as an attempt to place regulated Hong Kong dollar money closer to applications that might need it. The collaboration creates a route to wider distribution. Actual issuance, access conditions and repeated customer use will show how much of that opportunity becomes a functioning market. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
